Q021-01.notes: q = (4/3)p; q - p = p/3 = 5 so p = 15 (q = 20). Two routine steps.

Q021-02.notes: 2x-5 = ax+7 gives x = 12/(2-a) < 0, so a > 2. Only a = 4 works (x = -6). Checked: a=-3 gives x=2.4, a=0 gives 6, a=1 gives 12. Students can also graph each choice.

Q021-03.notes: f(9) = 6 + b = 1 so b = -5; f(-3) = -2 - 5 = -7. Distractor -5 is b.

Q021-04.notes: small = 3L; 9L + 5L = 14L = 364 so L = 26 (78 small). Borderline easy/medium.

flags: minor: choice A (0) is trivially true as the launch time but the question clearly asks for the return time; most students will reject it, so it is a weak distractor
Q021-06.notes: h(0) = -18 + 50 = 32. The parabola is symmetric about t = 3, so h(6) = 32 as well; the answer is t = 6. Distractor 3 is the vertex time.

flags: minor: easy to solve by plugging in the choices (3 + 1/3 = 10/3), and the x > 1 condition eliminates 1/3 at once
Q021-07.notes: 3x^2 - 10x + 3 = 0 gives x = 3 or 1/3; x > 1 so x = 3.

Q021-08.notes: 1452/1200 = 1.21 = (1.1)^2, so the increase is 10% per year. Traps: 21 (total) or 10.5 (21/2).
